cold_open.hook: Nasdaq down 0.82% as Iran tensions spike—but TSMC just posted a 68% revenue surge that's making chipmakers look like the only adults in the room.

markets.macro_note: Risk-off on geopolitical flare-up; energy and enterprise software bid, semiconductors mixed despite TSMC strength.

big_story.story_title: TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, reports 68% surge in June revenue
big_story.angle: TSMC's monster June number (68% YoY) is the rare piece of hard demand signal in a market drowning in AI hype—what it actually tells us about whether the AI capex cycle is real or just a very expensive belief system.

quick_hits.angle: Nasdaq slide tied to fresh US-Iran strikes and SK Hynix plunge—geopolitical risk is now a live equity factor again, not just a talking point.
Big banks about to report record revenue on SpaceX IPO fees and war volatility—the financial system's best quarter is built on chaos and billionaire launches.
Europe moving to hard limits on teen social media use—the regulatory playbook that started with TikTok is now coming for Instagram and Snapchat, and it's actually sticking.
Paramount-WBD merger facing multi-state lawsuits before it even closes—consolidation in media is hitting a wall that even scale can't break through.

odd_thing.joke_angle: Lorde says Ray-Ban Meta AI glasses aren't sexy—a pop star just became the product reviewer that Meta's engineers didn't want to hear from, and she's right.

yesterday_callback.topic: Meta's up 5.3% on AI cloud dreams while Netflix drops 3%—the market's decided which streaming future it believes in.
yesterday_callback.fresh_take: Today: Meta's AI hardware (the glasses) is getting roasted by actual cultural tastemakers, not just investors—the gap between Meta's AI narrative and what people actually want to wear is widening fast.

sign_off.callback_target: TSMC's 68% surge—the one number today that doesn't need a story to justify itself.
